meta.title: Data lineage: where every piece of data comes from
meta.ref_base: Paths in ref, samples, path and impl are relative to the NASA PROJECT folder.

status_legend.live: Real data or a real working path: real devices, real public data, deterministic app code.
status_legend.simulated: Synthetic values or a simulated counterpart (fictional crew, link, wrist, ground).
status_legend.planned: Named in the design with a channel mapping, not connected.
status_legend.offline-sample: Real public feed, verified live on 2026-11-14, used only as a saved snapshot. The app makes no runtime external request.

extra_fields.ref: Files each claim comes from (every node and edge).
extra_fields.stage: build = Tomas's Python pipeline before the app loads; runtime = inside the web app.
extra_fields.impl: Code file. ml paths were checked on disk. Web paths follow the planned layout in BUILD-KICKOFF section 2 and were not checked.
extra_fields.samples: Saved responses in docs/research/samples (checked on disk).
extra_fields.maps_to: crew_data.json metric keys a planned device would feed.
extra_fields.relation: Set on edges that are not a plain forward data flow: parity-test, calibration-note, user-input, bus-publish (a later layer publishing to the shared bus), display (handoff summary shown back on the console). Every edge without a relation runs from a lower or equal layer to a higher one.
extra_fields.edge.status: Same vocabulary as node status, for that one link.

rules: Layers are one-way. The build-time crew pipeline sits in layer 0 because its output file stands in for the sensors.
No number that lives in crew_data.json or storm_forecast.json is repeated here. Read values from the files.
Real crew vitals are private (Privacy Act of 1974), so crew vitals are simulated with fictional crew.
Simulated vitals are never attached to real named astronauts.
GOES data describes space weather near Earth, not crew dose.
open_points: Environment dose rates in crew_data.json are working values set by hand; the Moon value is still to verify (THESIS-DETAILS section 7).
CBC study number: research says OSD-569, contract and real_crew.py say OSD-575.
CMO-DA and the DTN-style queue are described in BUILD-KICKOFF and THESIS only; no research file covers them.
No LOINC code found for mood (1-5), exercise, bone loss or dose; local codes needed.
Bio-Analyzer page names no analytes; glucose through it is a team mapping.

nodes.label: Astronaut
nodes.source: Self-report and self-measurement at the daily check-in
ref: docs/research/2-data-sources/04-prototype-data-sources.md section 1 (manual entry is allowed by the challenge)
nodes.note: Mood is self-report only (1-5 scale). Exercise comes from the exercise log.

nodes.label: BLE heart strap
nodes.source: Any chest strap or watch broadcasting the standard Bluetooth Heart Rate Service
nodes.license: Open standard (Bluetooth SIG GATT); no account, no cost
nodes.cadence: Notifications, about 1 per second (unverified per device)
nodes.note: Chrome, Edge, Opera and Chrome Android only. Needs HTTPS or localhost and a button click.

nodes.label: Bio-Monitor
nodes.source: CSA Bio-Monitor smart shirt and headband (Astroskin, Carre Technologies), on the ISS since December 2018
nodes.license: No public data; ground science team only
nodes.cadence: Recorded per session on a battery pack; batch downlink after docking
nodes.note: Listed in the device registry as not connected. Hexoskin BLE, SDK and REST routes were judged not practical in 48 h, so the channel is simulated.

nodes.label: Actiwatch
nodes.source: NASA Actiwatch Spectrum wrist actigraph (motion and ambient light)
nodes.cadence: Continuous wear; data access not stated
ref: docs/THESIS-DETAILS.md section 8 (sleep measured by wrist actigraphy)

nodes.label: T-Mini
nodes.source: ESA T-Mini (Thermo-Mini) headband core temperature sensor
nodes.cadence: Continuous wear; data access not stated
ref: docs/THESIS-DETAILS.md section 8 (temperature: headband sensor, T-Mini class)

nodes.label: Crew dosimeter
nodes.source: Crew-worn dosimeters: ESA Active Dosimeter, CSA EVARM pocket dosimeters
nodes.cadence: Dose over time; data access not stated

nodes.label: Bio-Analyzer
nodes.source: CSA Bio-Analyzer: blood, saliva, urine from a finger prick; goal 2 to 3 h to result
nodes.cadence: Per sample; result in 2 to 3 h (goal)
ref: docs/THESIS-DETAILS.md section 8 (glucose: finger prick on analyser)
nodes.note: The CSA page names no analytes such as glucose. Glucose via this path is a team mapping, entered through the manual check-in.

nodes.label: Published ranges
nodes.source: Published spaceflight physiology and clinical ranges used to seed the generator and the bands
nodes.license: Papers and agency pages cited per row in the research
ref: docs/THESIS-DETAILS.md section 8 (bands are Team or Clinical, never NASA; only the 600 mSv career limit is a NASA number)
contracts/DATA_CONTRACT.md (meta.note: simulated crew from published ranges)

nodes.label: Crew generator
nodes.source: ml/make_sample_data.py: AR(1) daily persistence with correlated shocks, planted demo days applied after the draw
ref: ml/results/synthetic_crew.md (approved correlation matrix, AR(1) coefficients, realized fidelity)
nodes.note: Bone loss and dose are built from the daily inputs and the planted storm day; they are not part of the correlation matrix. The storm dose sits on the one real GOES >10 MeV storm inside the mission window (date read from the file).

nodes.label: Baseline rule
nodes.source: ml/crew_flags.py: personal baseline from the first 14 days, z of the 3-day mean, low-side-only metrics, absolute limits
nodes.note: Reference implementation of the rule. core/scoring.ts must reproduce it exactly (rule parity test).

nodes.label: crew_data.json
nodes.source: web/public/data/crew_data.json, written by make_sample_data.py with flags from crew_flags.py
nodes.license: Team data; simulated, not real astronaut records
nodes.cadence: Regenerated by Tomas; the app must survive a regenerate with no code change

nodes.label: NASA DONKI
nodes.source: NASA CCMC DONKI event catalogue: FLR, CME, SEP (also GST, IPS, notifications)
nodes.license: No key, free; credit NASA CCMC DONKI (licence text not stated in the research)
nodes.cadence: Event catalogue; pulled at build time from 2010-01-01; suggested refresh 15 to 60 min; max 60 days per request
nodes.note: Use the direct CCMC host. api.nasa.gov DONKI FLR returned HTTP 404 and the legacy kauai host timed out on 2026-11-14. Real data, used at build time only; the app makes no runtime request.

nodes.label: NOAA scales
nodes.source: NOAA SWPC R, S, G scale levels now plus 3-day probabilities
nodes.license: No key, free (US government data; licence text not stated in the research)
nodes.cadence: Live; poll at most once per minute (cache-control max-age=60)
nodes.note: S level is the single radiation light. GOES describes geostationary orbit: label as space weather near Earth, not crew dose.

nodes.label: GOES protons
nodes.source: NOAA SWPC GOES integral proton flux, 5-minute steps; the >=10 MeV channel defines the S scale
nodes.license: No key, free (US government data; licence text not stated in the research)
nodes.cadence: 5 min; files for 6 hour, 1 day, 3 day, 7 day
ref: docs/THESIS-DETAILS.md section 7 (GOES >=10 MeV flux: real, optional bundled files, replay overlay)

nodes.label: GOES X-ray
nodes.source: NOAA SWPC GOES X-ray flares (latest, 7 day) and 1-minute X-ray flux
nodes.license: No key, free (US government data; licence text not stated in the research)
nodes.cadence: 1 min flux; flare list on event

nodes.label: SWPC alerts
nodes.source: NOAA SWPC text watches, warnings and alerts
nodes.license: No key, free (US government data; licence text not stated in the research)

nodes.label: Planetary Kp
nodes.source: NOAA SWPC planetary K index (3-hour, 1-minute estimate, forecast); second source GFZ Potsdam
nodes.license: No key, free; GFZ copy is CC BY 4.0
ref: docs/research/2-data-sources/01-realtime-data-apis.md sections 2.1 and 2.2 (no biological effect listed for G storms: context only)

nodes.label: iSWA HAPI dose
nodes.source: NASA CCMC iSWA HAPI: Curiosity RAD dose on Mars, LRO CRaTER dose in lunar orbit, GOES protons
nodes.license: No key, free (licence text not stated in the research)
nodes.cadence: MSL RAD about every 17 min, about 2 days behind; CRaTER about 5 weeks behind
nodes.note: Benchmark for the Moon and Mars dose rates. Units are absorbed dose (uGy/day, cGy/day), not effective dose (mSv).

nodes.label: OSDR RadLab
nodes.source: NASA OSDR RadLab: dose rates from ISS detectors (DosTel and others) and BioSentinel
nodes.license: No key, free; NASA SMD Science Information Policy
nodes.note: No CORS header: pre-download a slice. Benchmark for the ISS dose rate.

nodes.label: ISS Live
nodes.source: ISS Live public telemetry (Lightstreamer, adapter set ISSLIVE): cabin pressure, ppO2, ppCO2, cabin temperature, water tanks
nodes.license: No key, free; public demo server, not an SLA service
nodes.cadence: Push on change (MERGE mode); values can be days stale
nodes.note: No crew biomedical item, humidity or dose in the public list. Dictionary units do not match observed values; label units from observation.

nodes.label: ISS position
nodes.source: Where The ISS At: latitude, longitude, altitude, velocity, day or night
nodes.note: Context only: day and night cycle.

nodes.label: Crew roster
nodes.source: corquaid ISS APIs: people in space, expedition, craft
nodes.note: Context only. Never attach simulated vitals to real named astronauts.

nodes.label: Inspiration4 labs
nodes.source: NASA OSDR Inspiration4 blood panels: comprehensive metabolic panel (OSD-575) and complete blood count, 4 crew, 7 timepoints, with lab reference ranges
nodes.license: NASA SMD Science Information Policy; cite each study
nodes.cors: S3 bucket open; search API none
nodes.note: Real, de-identified, public. The research lists the CBC under OSD-569 and the metabolic panel under OSD-575; the contract and real_crew.py cite OSD-575 for both. Check before quoting the study number for the CBC.

nodes.label: fetch_donki.py
nodes.source: ml/fetch_donki.py: pulls DONKI FLR, CME, SEP; caches raw JSON; writes flares.csv, cmes.csv, seps.csv

nodes.label: real_crew.py
nodes.source: ml/real_crew.py: scores Inspiration4 CBC and chemistry against each person's pre-flight mean

nodes.label: Data loader
nodes.source: Loads the JSON files from public/data with types from the contract; precached by the service worker
ref: docs/BUILD-KICKOFF.md sections 2, 3 (fully offline) and 7 (Phase 0: types from the contract, loader)

nodes.label: ReplayAdapter
nodes.source: Replays crew_data.json series as Observations (the simulated crew, default source)
nodes.cadence: Simulated clock, one row per mission day

nodes.label: Check-in adapter
nodes.source: ManualCheckInAdapter: the daily check-in form becomes Observations

nodes.label: Bluetooth HR adapter
nodes.source: WebBluetoothHRAdapter: reads the standard Heart Rate Service behind a Connect strap button
nodes.note: Chrome only. First item to cut if late, after Ground view and Containerfile (BUILD-KICKOFF section 7).

nodes.label: Sim Bio-Monitor
nodes.source: SimBioMonitorAdapter: simulated Bio-Monitor-class channels
ref: docs/research/3-health-science/09-csa-bio-monitor.md (How to use this in the build: exactly its six channels)

nodes.label: Sim dosimeter
nodes.source: SimDosimeterAdapter: simulated personal dosimeter, dose rate from the environment plus storm spikes
ref: docs/research/2-data-sources/01-realtime-data-apis.md section 3.4 (simulated personal dosimeter; label simulated values as estimates)

nodes.label: Device registry
nodes.source: Lists every adapter with channels and status, including planned devices shown as not connected
ref: docs/BUILD-KICKOFF.md sections 2 (registry) and 3 (device swap: adapter contract test)

nodes.label: Space weather snapshot
nodes.source: Bundled SWPC snapshot for the replay overlay and the space-weather-now chip (optional scope)
nodes.cadence: Bundled at build; no runtime request
ref: docs/THESIS-DETAILS.md sections 7 and 13 (GOES overlay; NOAA chip with cached fallback: should)
nodes.note: Optional. The offline rule means bundled files, not live calls.

nodes.label: prepare_model_flares.py
nodes.source: ml/prepare_model_flares.py: M and X class only; label = DONKI link to a GOES >10 MeV SEP; drops flares inside a running storm

nodes.label: real_crew.json
nodes.source: web/public/data/real_crew.json: Inspiration4 lab draws scored against each person's pre-flight mean
nodes.license: NASA SMD Science Information Policy; cite OSDR
ref: contracts/DATA_CONTRACT.md (real_crew.json: not the simulated crew, not an input to the check-in scorer)

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.source: core/observation.ts: every reading normalized to one FHIR Observation-shaped record; LOINC codes only where verified
nodes.license: HL7 FHIR R4 (open standard); LOINC codes
ref: docs/research/2-data-sources/04-prototype-data-sources.md section 4 (FHIR R4 Observation and LOINC table)
nodes.note: No LOINC was found for the 1-5 mood scale or radiation dose: use local codes. Dose is environment data, not a patient Observation. Exercise and bone loss are not covered by the research table.

nodes.label: Event bus
nodes.source: core/bus.ts: small event store; every Observation, flag, alert and report passes through it
ref: docs/BUILD-KICKOFF.md sections 2 (core/bus.ts) and 5 (Systems diagram driven by real bus events)

nodes.label: Storm model v1
nodes.source: ml/train_v1.py: logistic regression fit on train only, thresholds chosen on validation, test years untouched until frozen
nodes.note: Model name, thresholds and headline numbers are read from storm_forecast.json meta, never retyped.

nodes.label: run_test_and_export.py
nodes.source: ml/run_test_and_export.py: scores 2024 to today with v1 and writes storm_forecast.json

nodes.label: storm_forecast.json
nodes.source: web/public/data/storm_forecast.json: real model output on held-out test flares
nodes.license: Team data derived from NASA CCMC DONKI; credit in meta.data_credit
nodes.cadence: Regenerated by Tomas; the app must survive a regenerate with no code change
nodes.note: Replay uses split == test events in the window the contract names. Headline numbers come only from meta.metrics_test.

nodes.label: Scoring
nodes.source: core/scoring.ts: personal-baseline rule, absolute limits, low-side-only metrics, dose and bone bands
ref: docs/BUILD-KICKOFF.md sections 2 (core/scoring.ts), 3 (rule parity with ml) and 4 (alert rule)
nodes.note: Deterministic. No generative AI in alerts or scoring.

nodes.label: Radiation
nodes.source: core/radiation.ts: forecast feed, alert levels, replay timeline, per-storm lead time, dose gauge against the career limit

nodes.label: Escalation
nodes.source: core/escalation.ts: status and environment decide who is told, the one-way delay and the report queue
ref: docs/BUILD-KICKOFF.md sections 2 (core/escalation.ts) and 4 (verify step, escalation, environment switch)

nodes.label: Crew Console
nodes.source: Main surface: crew overview, body map, metric panel, check-in, action, re-measure, escalation

nodes.label: Radiation module
nodes.source: Dose gauge, forecast feed, model card and the May 2024 replay

nodes.label: Wrist
nodes.source: Simulated watch face docked on screen: urgency pulses only; real vibration where navigator.vibrate is supported

nodes.label: Systems
nodes.source: Architecture map and flight-readiness checks, driven by bus events; this file is its data model

nodes.label: Crew medical officer
nodes.source: Crew member acting as medical officer on board; told at once on red

nodes.label: CMO-DA handoff
nodes.source: core/handoff.ts: builds the case bundle (JSON) and a plain-language summary from a deterministic template
nodes.cadence: On demand, from any amber or red

nodes.label: CMO-DA
nodes.source: NASA JSC Crew Medical Officer Digital Assistant: offline AI medic, built with Google, tested with Red Hat on a ground copy of HPE Spaceborne Computer-2, not yet flown
nodes.note: No integration exists. Label the output: Prepared for an onboard AI medical assistant such as NASA's CMO-DA. This item is not covered in docs/research/; the source is the thesis and the kickoff file.

nodes.label: Link queue
nodes.source: core/link.ts: comm-link simulator with delay by environment, loss-of-signal windows and a store-and-forward queue (DTN-style bundles)
ref: docs/BUILD-KICKOFF.md sections 2 (core/link.ts) and 3 (link delay and loss, downlink budget)
docs/THESIS-DETAILS.md sections 2 (row 4) and 3 (one-way delay by environment)
nodes.note: Simulated link, not a real DTN stack. Delay values come from core/link.ts with their sources in THESIS-DETAILS; bare light time and operational latency differ for the Moon.

nodes.label: Ground
nodes.source: Flight surgeon view: reports arriving after the one-way delay, link status, what the crew already did
nodes.note: First item to cut if late (BUILD-KICKOFF section 7).

nodes.label: Flight surgeon
nodes.source: Flight surgeon at mission control; sees crew health data privately in real practice
nodes.cadence: After the link delay; amber waits for the next private medical conference
ref: docs/research/2-data-sources/01-realtime-data-apis.md section 5.2 (private medical conference, who sees crew data)
